correctness.rationale: Rank-pair counting, Gaussian q-product normalizer, total-variation coupling, sharp one-defect coefficient and two-subspace rare-tail estimate have been reconstructed for all n>=1, fixed prime-power q>=2, with explicit parity conditions. A standalone direct finite-field matrix-pair verifier passed 5 exhaustive configurations and 48 exact symbolic identities. Finite checks support formulas but do not prove limits.

evidence: Đurić–Jevđenić–Stopar, arXiv:1810.02776, Proposition 3.1 gives the outdegree by Gaussian-binomial subspace counts in the compressed digraph of image–kernel classes; it neither weighs each class by the number of matrices nor analyzes the joint-uniform rank distribution as n grows at fixed q.
Huang, arXiv:2110.15566, §3.1 equations (3.1)–(3.5) counts ordered pairs with both AB=0 and BA=0, not the one-sided relation.
Gould, Johnson and Naz, arXiv:1907.12518, classify Green rank strata and study regularity/Fountain conditions for matrix semigroups but do not derive a zero-product pair law.
Published mathematical record “Zero-insertive matrices are exactly the half-rank locus” (2026) characterizes a half-rank property of individual matrices, not pair-uniform random products.
broader_coverage.reasoning: The mutually annihilating problem imposes BA=0 as an extra condition, changing the compatible second-map fiber from q^{n(n-r)} to q^{(n-r)^2}; it therefore cannot imply the stated normalized distribution. General rank Green-strata are useful for counting but do not contain the fixed-q asymptotic or the precise homology tail. The compressed-graph degree formula gives the unweighted rank adjacency structure, not the probability measure obtained by lifting to actual ordered matrices; the q-theta and first-homology asymptotics are not derived there.

evidence: Catanzaro and Zabka, arXiv:1901.00964, Lemma 2.5 and Definition 3.1, condition the second map after the first; their Theorem B sends field size to infinity, with no joint-uniform fixed-field theta statement.

Sequentially conditional sampling does not implement that weighting. The one-map equation D²=0 is a different parameter space. No equivalent joint-parity law was found in the inspected literature.

originality.rationale: Compared the proposed joint-uniform AB=0 theorem with primary full-text work on finite-field compressed zero-divisor digraphs, matrix monoids, sequential random chain complexes, mutually annihilating AB=BA=0 pairs, and one square-zero differential D²=0. Their parameter spaces/conditioning differ materially, or their theorems do not imply the fixed-q n-growing theta limit and defect coefficient. Available searches do not establish universal priority; quiver-equivalence risk is retained.
residual_risks: A compressed-graph adjacency formula in Đurić–Jevđenić–Stopar is a finite-level precursor; it may have been asymptotically analyzed in uninspected follow-up work.
A historically published theorem on point counts or random representations of the A3 quiver with path-length-two relation may imply the exact limit in a different notation.
Only relevant accessible primary material and indexed searches were inspected, not a complete bibliography or independent literature audit.

value.rationale: The zero-product relation governs ordered edges in a natural finite matrix semigroup; rank is its canonical Green stratification. The result finds a dimension-growing theta profile for a jointly uniform compatible pair, a near-certain exact middle term and a sharp parity-dependent exponentially small defect, sharply distinguishing sequential sampling and the known D²=0 model. These are nontrivial structural asymptotics, not merely rephrased elementary finite enumeration.
